# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations under the EU AI Act has changed since original adoption. While Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 initially set 2 August 2026 as the applicable date, a subsequent amending regulation (the "AI Omnibus," Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) extended this to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). Many commentary and legal-analysis sources have not yet been updated to reflect this change, creating a significant risk of outdated compliance guidance circulating in the market.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
As originally adopted in June 2024, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 provided that Annex III high-risk AI system obligations (Chapter III, Sections 1–3) would become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e. on 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Commission's legislative proposal for the Digital Package on Simplification, known as the "AI Omnibus," was adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). Political agreement between the Council and the European Parliament on the amendments, including the delay for Annex III obligations, was reached on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The AI Omnibus regulation (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) subsequently entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

This amendment extended the application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations from 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Under the amended Article 113(c), Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (with the exception of Article 6(5)) shall apply from this new date (medium confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### Related Deadlines
The Omnibus also extended the application date for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I, e.g. machinery, toys, lifts) to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Importantly, the original 2 August 2026 date remains in force for other obligations, such as Article 50 transparency duties, AI literacy requirements, and certain prohibitions — but not for the Annex III high-risk obligations specifically (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [euaicompass.com](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

Multiple sources present conflicting dates for Annex III obligations. The EU's own Article 111 guidance page still references 2 August 2026, apparently not yet updated to reflect the Omnibus amendment, while the official FAQ page confirms 2 December 2027. Similarly, several commentary and legal-analysis sources describe 2 August 2026 as the operative or imminent deadline without reflecting the later extension (medium confidence) ([artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). This appears to be a case of outdated sources not yet reflecting the amendment, rather than a genuine legal contradiction.

One pre-Omnibus source characterized 2 December 2027 as merely a proposed "backstop" date contingent on timely legislative approval (low confidence, 0.12) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)); this contingency has since been resolved by the Omnibus's entry into force.

A separate low-confidence claim (0.12) asserting that high-risk AI systems require an "algorithm passport" registered with the AI Office is uncorroborated by any other source and should not be treated as an established legal requirement ([ai-compliance-hub.example](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist)).

## Knowledge Gaps

- The exact current consolidated text of Article 113 post-Omnibus is not fully available from the sources reviewed.
- It is unclear whether Article 6(5) has its own distinct, separate application timeline.
- It is not confirmed whether the AI Office or national regulators have issued further guidance on enforcement flexibility beyond the stated dates.
- No information is available on possible sector-specific or Member State-level derogations affecting enforcement timing.

While Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 initially set 2 August 2026 as the applicable date, a subsequent amending regulation (the "AI Omnibus," Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) extended this to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). Many commentary and legal-analysis sources have not yet been updated to reflect this change, creating a significant risk of outdated compliance guidance circulating in the market.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
As originally adopted in June 2024, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 provided that Annex III high-risk AI system obligations (Chapter III, Sections 1–3) would become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e. on 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Commission's legislative proposal for the Digital Package on Simplification, known as the "AI Omnibus," was adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). Political agreement between the Council and the European Parliament on the amendments, including the delay for Annex III obligations, was reached on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The AI Omnibus regulation (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) subsequently entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

This amendment extended the application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations from 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Under the amended Article 113(c), Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (with the exception of Article 6(5)) shall apply from this new date (medium confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### Related Deadlines
The Omnibus also extended the application date for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I, e.g. machinery, toys, lifts) to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Importantly, the original 2 August 2026 date remains in force for other obligations, such as Article 50 transparency duties, AI literacy requirements, and certain prohibitions — but not for the Annex III high-risk obligations specifically (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [euaicompass.com](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

Multiple sources present conflicting dates for Annex III obligations. The EU's own Article 111 guidance page still references 2 August 2026, apparently not yet updated to reflect the Omnibus amendment, while the official FAQ page confirms 2 December 2027. Similarly, several commentary and legal-analysis sources describe 2 August 2026 as the operative or imminent deadline without reflecting the later extension (medium confidence) ([artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). This appears to be a case of outdated sources not yet reflecting the amendment, rather than a genuine legal contradiction.

One pre-Omnibus source characterized 2 December 2027 as merely a proposed "backstop" date contingent on timely legislative approval (low confidence, 0.12) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)); this contingency has since been resolved by the Omnibus's entry into force.

A separate low-confidence claim (0.12) asserting that high-risk AI systems require an "algorithm passport" registered with the AI Office is uncorroborated by any other source and should not be treated as an established legal requirement ([ai-compliance-hub.example](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist)).

## Knowledge Gaps

- The exact current consolidated text of Article 113 post-Omnibus is not fully available from the sources reviewed.
- It is unclear whether Article 6(5) has its own distinct, separate application timeline.
- It is not confirmed whether the AI Office or national regulators have issued further guidance on enforcement flexibility beyond the stated dates.
- No information is available on possible sector-specific or Member State-level derogations affecting enforcement timing.
